subject: Invariance test MLM: lavaan WARNING: scaling factor is negative

messages.author: 71456cfe2b31001e
messages.subject: Invariance test MLM: lavaan WARNING: scaling factor is negative
parts:
Hello,

I want to test which item(s) I need to free (unconstrain) to achieve partial measurement invariance. Because my data is not multivariate normal distributed, I correct for it:

model2 <- measurementInvariance(model.DV, data=df, group="COO", std.lv = TRUE, estimator = "MLM", se = "robust", test = "Satorra-Bentler")
partialInvariance(model2, type = "strong", p.adjust = "holm", free = c()) #

However, I get 13 times the same warning message: 
Warning messages:
1: In lav_test_diff_SatorraBentler2001(mods[[m]], mods[[m +  ... :
  lavaan WARNING: scaling factor is negative
2: ...


Moreover, when looking at the free.chi and free.p items, three of them are "NA". When I allow the intercepts of the three items to remain unconstrain (free = c() ), the model fit increases and is partially invariant. Is it safe to ignore the warning messages? Running the SEMs (combined or separately for each group) is fine, without warning messages. Also, looking at the loadings instead of the intercepts (i.e., replacing type = "strong" with type = "weak") does not result in the warnings.
Replacing estimator = "MLM" by "ML" or deleting se = or test = still results in the same warning messages.

Thank you
Paul

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Invariance test MLM: lavaan WARNING: scaling factor is negative
parts:
I don't have much to offer without knowing anything about your model or data, but you could try setting method = "satorra.bentler.2010" to use a test statistic that is guaranteed positive (although I'm not sure if that has anything to do with a negative scaling factor). 

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

parts:
Thanks for your answer Terrence. I have added method = "satorra.bentler.2010" but the warning messages keep appearing.
My model is rather simple:
model <- '
  # measurement model
  IV1 =~ JD1 + JD2 + JP1 + JP2 + JP3 + JI1 + JI2
  IV2 =~ EPE1 + EPE2 + EPE3
  IV3 =~ SRS1 + SRS2
  DV =~ LC1 + LC2 + LA1 + LA2 + LA3
  # regression
  DV ~ IV3
  IV3 ~ IV1 + IV2
  '

As said before, when I change type = "strong" to type = "weak" the warning messages disappear. All items are positively correlated (range: .06 to .80).
Maybe it is a problem that I run partialInvariance(model, ...) for the whole SEM instead multiple CFAs? However, I have done this before for other models and data and it worked fine. Changing the model structure (e.g., all IVs as predictors without moderator) did also result in the same warning messages.

messages.author: af82fa98896529e2
messages.subject: Re: Invariance test MLM: lavaan WARNING: scaling factor is negative
parts:
All measurement invariance functions were not designed for structural model. All latent variables must be correlated. This might be the problem you found.

Regarding to the NA in partialInvariance, it does occur a lot, usually in fix columns. This is probably that the likelihood ratio test does not provide satisfactory results. I recommend you to see the statistics of all types, as well as your theory, to justify which variables are candidate to be freely estimated across groups.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Invariance test MLM: lavaan WARNING: scaling factor is negative
parts:
I would recommend running these models (configural/weak/strong)
manually. You can use labels to constrain sets of parameters to be equal
across groups, see: http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html

For example, strong invariance for the Holzinger & Swineford model can
be specified as follows:

HS.model.strong <- '
visual =~ c(1,1)*x1 + c(l2, l2)*x2 + c(l3, l3)*x3
textual =~ c(1,1)*x4 + c(l5, l5)*x5 + c(l6, l6)*x6
speed =~ c(1,1)*x7 + c(l8, l8)*x8 + c(l9, l9)*x9

# ov intercepts
x1 ~ c(i1, i1)*1
x2 ~ c(i2, i2)*1
x3 ~ c(i3, i3)*1
x4 ~ c(i4, i4)*1
x5 ~ c(i5, i5)*1
x6 ~ c(i6, i6)*1
x7 ~ c(i7, i7)*1
x8 ~ c(i8, i8)*1
x9 ~ c(i9, i9)*1

# lv means
visual ~ c(0, NA)*1
textual ~ c(0, NA)*1
speed ~ c(0, NA)*1
'

fit.strong <- cfa(HS.model.strong, data = HolzingerSwineford1939,
group = "school")

Comparing the models can be done using the anova() function, or (if you
need more options), the lavTestLRT() function.

Next, you can allow for partial invariance by setting some equal labels
to be unequal. For example, for the factor loading of x2, you can write

c(l2, l2bis)*x2

And then, you can compare the models again using anova/lavTestLRT.

This will make it more clear what is causing the NAs.

Yves.
